contexts.description: Fundamental rules for all code generation: readability, intent-revealing naming, declarative-over-imperative style, resource cleanup, async-first concurrency. Relevant to any task that writes or designs code.

Required engineering practices for moderately sized or complex codebases: data modeling, tests, external-data ingestion, error/exception handling, cross-system integration, installable/deployable packages.
Required practices for addressing linting, type-checking, and formatting issues. Relevant when the plan touches lint/type/format tooling or fixing such findings.
How to effectively run shell/terminal commands, virtualenvs, and output piping. Relevant when the plan involves running commands, scripts, or CLI tools.
Structuring code so its control flow reads as a top-down narrative. Relevant when the plan authors or substantially restructures non-trivial code.
